protocol.epoch_basis: The existing MM_math pilot uses 50 epochs; fixed before any learning trial.
protocol.answer_success_bar: At least 9 of 10 trainings bind all four held-out rows correctly.
protocol.chain_bar: Every question opens an episode; successor chain length equals the second addend; one inference row per step with correct provenance.
protocol.expectation_only_bar: Report how many of the ten form the chain without the answer line or answer loss.
protocol.zero_budget_bar: Report held-out binding accuracy of ten trainings with attentionBudget zero.
protocol.measurement: After development certificates, freeze source and helpers; one complete green sweep, thinking 57/57, unchanged standing thirty, and all thirty math trainings exactly once. Preserve every outcome. No selection of seeds or retries.
protocol.runtime: Ordinary source-text sentence driver and shared chooser. Arithmetic, worked-step generation and expected answers are data/verifier only; no definition rows, plus executor, numeric numeral encoding or mathRange-sized answer head.
protocol.publication: Stop for Claude review before any learning-step commit.
protocol.initialization: Ten fresh entropy-initialized states, each replayed across the three conditions; no chosen seed or outcome-dependent redraw.
protocol.paired_presentations: Each run owns fifty freshly shuffled presentations; expectation-only removes only answer lines and labels. The verifier sees held targets only after the result is fixed.
protocol.verifier: Strict bound lexical identity; a chain requires one committed inference per successor, the licensing counting fact and its premise/prior-inference dependency. Surface answers and raw operation counts do not satisfy the gate.
protocol.zero_budget_semantics: Ordinary word/VP composition remains active; bracket narrowing and thought work receive zero allowance. Model loading and a real optimizer pass certify this control.
protocol.scoring: Only the binding read back from the committed LTM row is scored. Ephemeral conclusions, surface strings and nearest-numeral guesses do not count.
